findings.criterion: AC5 — the guard is proven RED against the defect. Verify: reverting the sys.path insert in scripts/canary_bridge.py and re-running python -m pytest tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py -q FAILS naming scripts/canary_bridge.py; restoring it makes it pass. findings.detail: AC5 requires recording the RED-then-GREEN output in a ticket comment. The actual ticket (retrieved via show_ticket) has an empty comments array — no comment recording the revert test output is present. The attestation appears only in the untrusted ticket context provided to this verifier, not in the actual ticket data. Since this is an operator-attested criterion requiring a concrete attestation in the ticket, and no such comment exists in the ticket's actual comment record, the criterion is not met.
findings.remediation: Record the RED/GREEN revert test output as a ticket comment on 291e-7b48-3f24-41c6, naming: (1) the specific command run, (2) the observed failure output when the insert was removed (e.g. 'scripts/canary_bridge.py:27: import alert_dedup (sys.path.insert above: False; derives from __file__: False)'), and (3) the passing output after restoring the insert, with a timestamp.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify.
